title: Effects of Strength Training on Running Economy in Highly Trained Runners: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis of Controlled Trials
authors: Balsalobre-Fernandez C, Santos-Concejero J, Grivas GV
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: Competitive middle- and long-distance runners with VO2max above 60 ml/kg/min; 5 controlled trials
findings: Five controlled trials with 93 high-level middle- and long-distance runners met the criteria after 699 articles were screened; programs lasted longer than 4 weeks.

Four of the 5 studies used low to moderate intensities (40-70% 1RM) and all used low to moderate volume (2-4 lower-body resistance exercises plus up to 200 jumps and 5-10 short sprints), 2-3 times per week for 8-12 weeks.
Pooled effect on running economy was large and beneficial: SMD -1.42 (95% CI -2.23 to -0.60).
Authors conclude that low to high intensity resistance plus plyometric exercises 2-3 times per week for 8-12 weeks is an appropriate strategy for highly trained runners.
limitations: Only five small trials; very wide confidence interval; the pooled SMD is probably inflated by small samples and heterogeneous running-economy protocols; elite-only population (VO2max above 60) may not transfer to recreational runners; no performance outcome.
implications: Default strength block of 8-12 weeks, 2-3 sessions per week, 2-4 lower-body exercises plus a limited jump and short-sprint component (up to about 200 jumps per session as observed in the included trials).
Treat the SMD of -1.42 as an upper bound and do not use it to predict an individual's economy or pace gain; use the smaller Llanos-Lagos 2024 and Denadai 2017 estimates.

verification.notes: Crossref title, journal, 2016 and first author match. All numbers in abstract.
